title: Staggered toolchain init and quiet release prober
author: Riley Chen
release_notes: Introduce tiered toolchain bootstrap to reduce presubmit latency and add a non-blocking 'quiet' release prober that validates artifacts and flags regressions without blocking rollouts unless configured to escalate.
description: Summary: Introduces a staggered toolchain initialization flow and a lightweight release prober to reduce noisy presubmit and release flakiness while improving developer feedback time. Motivation: CI latency and flakiness spike during full toolchain boot (terraform/pyenv/npm installs) on large changes. Teams reported long presubmit warmups and occasional release-blocking transient failures that are expensive to triage. This PR decomposes bootstrap into three phases (minimal, background, final) and adds a quiet release prober that runs a minimal set of deterministic sanity checks post-build. Key changes: 1) toolchain/bootstrap/phase-0.sh - minimal runtime needed for quick presubmit checks; 2) toolchain/bootstrap/phase-1-bg.sh - background fetch/restore of heavy devdeps with resilient retry/backoff; 3) toolchain/bootstrap/phase-2-final.sh - completes remaining optional setup and writes a lockstamp for reproducibility; 4) .github/workflows/presubmit.yml - split presubmit into fastpath (phase-0) and slowpath (phase-1 background scheduled) lanes; 5) tools/release/prober.py - quiet release prober that runs deterministic smoke tests and artifact checks and reports to CI telemetry without hard-blocking by default; 6) scripts/ci/warm-cache.sh - warmed caches for node/python layers; 7) tests/smoke/release_smoke.py - harness for prober. Commits summary: - c1a9fa2: introduce phase-0 bootstrap and fastpath presubmit lane; - 9b2d4e1: implement background phase-1 boot sequence and resume semantics; - e7f3b8c: add release prober, telemetry hooks, and non-blocking reporting; - 4a6d33a: docs and examples + adjust presubmit workflow conditions. Files changed (high level): toolchain/bootstrap/* (new scripts), .github/workflows/presubmit.yml (refactor), tools/release/prober.py (new), scripts/ci/warm-cache.sh (modest additions), tests/smoke/* (new), docs/dev/toolchain.md (clarify phases). Tests & CI: All presubmit checks passed after iterating on flaky network fetch logic. CI matrix: build: pass; lint: pass; unit-tests: pass; integration-smoke: pass; e2e-release-smoke: pass. Performance: Median presubmit cold-start reduced from ~240s to ~95s on sampled Linux runners; steady-state developer feedback improved in local trials. Rollout plan: staged opt-in across teams via repo-level boolean flag (ci.toolchain.staggered=true) then orgwide flip after 2 weeks of telemetry. The release prober is non-blocking by default; ops can set RELEASE_PROBER_ENFORCE=true in release workflows to escalate failures. Review conversation (high level): - Ava Martinez (reviewer): "Nice decomposition, can we make phase-1 background retries exponential and cap disk usage?" - Riley Chen (author): "Added exponential backoff with jitter and a disk footprint cap; background tasks will clean temp caches older than 7 days." - Jordan Patel (reviewer): "Please add a README for maintainers and make telemetry tag names consistent with ci.tooling.*" - Riley Chen (author): "Added docs/dev/toolchain.md and normalized telemetry keys to ci.tooling.toolchain.*" - Samir Gupta (reviewer): "Would like a toggle to opt-out specific repos during rollout." - Riley Chen: "Added ci.toolchain.staggered=false opt-out and an org-level opt-in recommendation in the PR description." Requested changes: enforce more aggressive timeout for phase-0 fetches (addressed), robust handling of intermittent network 429s (addressed by retry + exponential backoff), and clearer log lines for prober failures (addressed). Approvals: Ava Martinez approved, Jordan Patel approved after changes, Samir Gupta approved with minor comments. Merge notes: Squash-merged to main after last CI run succeeded. Post-merge actions: 1) monitor ci.telemetry.tooling.presubmit_latency for spike regressions; 2) run org-level opt-in on a canary team for one week; 3) schedule a follow-up PR to add a quiet-mode dashboard and automated throttle heuristics if background boot persists. Related: ENG-4527 (reduce presubmit TTR), ENG-4590 (quiet rollout validation). Impact: reduces developer iteration cost and isolates heavy devdeps from fast presubmit lanes while providing safer, low-noise release verification. Rollback plan: flip ci.toolchain.staggered=false and revert presubmit workflow change if unexpected regressions occur.
